solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: 1940s swinger's cheers returned by male police officer

parts.note: HE is the male pronoun
PC is short for police constable

indicators.note: returned means the word for cheers is read backwards

parts.note: TA is British informal for thanks, i.e. cheers

explanation.surface: A wartime jazz fan's cheers are echoed back by a male constable.
explanation.definitionFit: A hepcat was a hip jazz or swing enthusiast in 1940s slang.

clue.text: Eg native of Wick taking school exam without gain?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the exam goes around the gain

parts.note: a Higher is a Scottish school exam, roughly the A level
to land something is to gain it, as in landing a job

explanation.surface: A Wick resident passes an exam with nothing to show for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Wick is a town in the far north of Scotland, so its natives are Highlanders; the Higher is the Scottish school exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the Scottish Highlands, such as a person born in Wick, is a Highlander.

clue.text: Formal setting for a Trojan king

indicators.note: a setting holds a jewel, so the word for formal encloses the letter

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal and proper

explanation.surface: A formal setting suited to a Trojan monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the king of Troy during the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Mean to declare advancing years?

parts.note: to aver is to declare or assert
to age is to advance in years

explanation.surface: Does one intend to announce that one is getting older?
explanation.definitionFit: The mean of a set of numbers is its arithmetic average.

clue.text: Situation thus involving Asian country backed by church

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the word for thus wraps the rest

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: backed means the country's name is read backwards

parts.note: Iran is a country in western Asia

explanation.surface: A political situation in which an Asian state has a church's support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' signals the reversal of the country's name; 'involving' puts church and reversed country inside the word for thus.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a possible state of affairs or sequence of events, a situation.

clue.text: Inexpensive headgear worn by ambassador

indicators.note: a hat is worn around the head, so the headgear encloses the ambassador

parts.note: a cap is a piece of headgear
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A cheap hat sported by a diplomat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cheap costs little, the plain sense of inexpensive.

clue.text: Poet messed around with and getting writer's block?

indicators.note: letters messed around with are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A poet fooling around ends up with writer's block.
explanation.walkthrough: Writer's block is the creative slump; read literally it is a block of paper a writer uses.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is a block of sheets for writing on, punningly a writer's block.

clue.text: Unemotional son leaves, given refresher course

indicators.note: leaves means the letter for son departs from the word

parts.note: restrained means holding emotion in check
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A cold son walks out after being sent on a refresher course.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrained means taught again, as on a refresher course to update skills.

clue.text: Outstanding work of Pindar possibly read aloud

indicators.note: read aloud signals that the word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: Pindar was an ancient Greek poet famous for odes

explanation.surface: An outstanding Greek poem may be recited.
explanation.definitionFit: Money outstanding is still owed, unpaid.

clue.text: Sentence about everything a booby may produce?

parts.note: bird, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time, is a prison sentence
C is circa, about
all means everything

explanation.surface: A prison term for everything a fool might do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booby' looks like a fool, but here it is a seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: A booby is a tropical seabird, so its cry is a bird call.

clue.text: Recommendation of good Scottish priest born in Paris

parts.note: guid is the Scots form of good
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
née is French for born

explanation.surface: A Scottish priest born in Paris recommends something good.
explanation.definitionFit: A guideline is an advisory rule, a recommendation on how to act.

clue.text: Student workers' association given support on course

parts.note: TU is a trade union
a golf ball sits on a tee on the course

explanation.surface: A student union backed by help with the course.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutee is a student who is taught by a tutor.

clue.text: Mood palpably altered with two rooks in tree

indicators.note: altered means the letters are changed into a new arrangement

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook, twice

explanation.surface: A chess game's mood visibly shifts once both rooks are in play.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lombardy poplar is a tall narrow tree, a variety of black poplar.

clue.text: Insect I see around lakes at end of March?

indicators.note: at end of puts what follows after the word for march

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: around means the word see is wrapped round the lakes

parts.note: L is short for lake, twice for lakes

explanation.surface: An insect spotted near lakes as March closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month but is a protest march.
explanation.definitionFit: Demoiselle is a name for a damselfly, a slender insect.

clue.text: Gunpowder constituent soldiers can put back at front

indicators.note: at front places the reversed can before the soldiers
put back means the word for can is reversed

parts.note: a tin is a can
RE are the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Troops stash the explosive ingredient back at the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre, potassium nitrate or saltpetre, is the oxidiser in gunpowder.

clue.text: Neat cover for Indonesian island's ethnicity

indicators.note: the word for neat covers, so encloses, the island

parts.note: trim means neat and tidy
Bali is an Indonesian island, with the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A tidy front for an Indonesian island's ethnic identity.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribalism is strong loyalty to one's own tribe or ethnic group, an ethnic identity.

clue.text: Profusion of bakery product served during a social

indicators.note: served during puts the bun inside the event

parts.note: a dance is a social gathering
a bun is a small bread roll or cake from a bakery

explanation.surface: Lots of buns are handed round at a social.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance is a great quantity, a profusion.

clue.text: Smooth out articles in French about old card game

indicators.note: about means the articles go round the card game

parts.note: un and le are French articles
ruff was an old card game, ancestor of whist

explanation.surface: French grammar articles discussing a forgotten card game.
explanation.definitionFit: To unruffle is to smooth or calm what was ruffled.

clue.text: Paul was one, always carrying weapon

indicators.note: carrying means the word for always holds the weapon

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always
a pistol is a weapon

explanation.surface: Saint Paul is pictured as forever armed.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Paul wrote many New Testament epistles, so he was a letter writer.

clue.text: Some thought it a nice old vessel!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone once admired a famous ship, with irony given its fate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titanic was the liner that sank in 1912, a famous old ship.

clue.text: Tragic day briefly captured in very old film

indicators.note: captured in means the shortened day sits inside the two letters
briefly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the Ides of March was the day Julius Caesar was murdered

explanation.surface: A tragic day is caught in an old film clip.
explanation.definitionFit: A video is a recorded film or moving picture.

clue.text: Retired priest is second to identify Puccinian style

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word for priest is reversed

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a priest
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A retired priest needs a moment to spot Puccini's manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Verismo is the realist Italian opera style of Puccini and Mascagni.

clue.text: Stuck with animal coat, promises to pay, being very quick

parts.note: fast means firmly stuck, as in stuck fast
and means with, together
fur is an animal's coat
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: Someone saddled with a fur coat and debts is in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast and furious means at great speed and intensity, idiomatically very quick.

clue.text: Like hooter US space administrators lacked at first

parts.note: NASA is the US space agency

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of lacked

explanation.surface: NASA once lacked a horn, perhaps for a launch.
explanation.walkthrough: A hooter is British slang for the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal means relating to the nose, which a hooter is in slang.

clue.text: Basket-maker, or provider of stockings in Albert Square?

indicators.note: in a Cockney accent the leading H is dropped

parts.note: a hosier sells stockings and socks

explanation.surface: A basket weaver or a stocking seller in an East London square.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Square is the setting of EastEnders, a London soap, whose Cockney characters drop their Hs.
explanation.definitionFit: Osier is willow whose pliant twigs are woven into baskets.

clue.text: Look out! It's planted with explosives, we're told!

indicators.note: we're told signals that the word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: a mined area has explosives buried in it

explanation.surface: A warning: the place is booby-trapped, so we hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Mind! is a British warning to take care, equivalent to look out!

clue.text: Revolutionary figure, one about to entertain team

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the pair surrounds the team

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
on means about, concerning
XI is eleven, a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A revolutionary leader plans to host a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests a rebel, but Ixion was bound to a turning wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Ixion was punished by being bound to an ever-turning fiery wheel.

clue.text: Shop assistant is large and extremely slothful, sadly

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters are put into a sorry disorder
extremely means just the outermost letters of slothful

explanation.surface: A shop worker described cruelly as big and very lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A salesgirl is a young woman who serves customers in a shop.

clue.text: Residence of Catholic dignitary in charge of French island

parts.note: Dom is a title given to some Catholic clergy, such as Benedictine monks
île is French for island

explanation.surface: A church dignitary's home, overseeing a French island.
explanation.definitionFit: A domicile is a person's home, their place of residence.

clue.text: 1 down's circular hollow in TV soap, familiarly

definitions.meaning: a Scottish name for a cirque, a round mountain hollow
The nickname of Coronation Street, a long-running British TV soap

explanation.surface: A Highlander's mountain hollow appears in a TV drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrie is Gaelic-derived Scots for a glacial cirque, and the familiar name of Coronation Street.
